text:
elaine: Heads-up — on the canary last night we saw a spike where full request bodies were captured for tenant 'acme-inc' even though their route sampling is set to 0.01. :eyes:

devon: saw the same. the request-capture flag appears to have been toggled by the debug-runner path during canary. short log excerpt: ```[INFO] debug-runner: capture=true tenant=acme route=/chat v=1.3.2```

ashok: hmm — debug-runner intentionally bypasses pre-scrub path to keep raw payloads for short-lived debug sessions. we thought that only applied to internal test tenants. did canary inherit that behavior?

elaine: looks like the canary switch flipped a temp-exempt for all tenants, not just internal. that was my bad when I merged the toggle defaults.

claire: UX note: we need a safer canary experience. suggest making the debug-exempt TTLed and visible in Console with a clear "captures raw payloads" badge. people shouldn't have to read deploy diffs to know this.

quentin: cost/quotas risk — if someone ramps canary capture for <100 tenants it blows out logs billing. we should add a quota guard and an alert that fires when capture volume > X req/min for non-internal tenants.

devon: agree. quick mitigation: roll back the canary default and patch debug-runner to only opt-in per-tenant via an explicit header `X-Debug-Inspect: true`.

ashok: technical detail: the scrubber runs in the post-router middleware. debug-runner bypasses middleware earlier, so even if scrub config is enabled we never hit it. patch idea: move minimal PII scrub (email/ssn masking) to an earlier sanitization pass that always runs before capture decision. full scrub can remain downstream.

elaine: proposed action items:
- rollback canary default (devon)
- add per-tenant opt-in header + fail-safe TTL (ashok)
- early-pass scrub for high-risk fields (ashok)
- console badge + per-route capture indicator + quick rollback CTA (claire)
- metric + quota alert for capture volume (quentin)

devon: rolled back the canary default at 03:12 UTC (prod). deploy-bot: canary reverse complete. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: deploy 2025.03.19-03:12 by devops triggered: canary defaults reset for debug-runner.

quentin: I'll add a Grafana panel for "raw-capture-reqs/min" and create an alert rule at 10 req/min per non-internal tenant. propose linked alert to a small oncall runbook.

claire: for Console UX — we should show a per-route "debug capture" toggle (read-only until you have admin), and a TTL field with countdown. lets mock a quick wireframe next week in PM sync.

ashok: implementing early-pass scrub now. quick regex-based mask for emails + cc numbers + SSN patterns; will ship behind a feature flag. sample config we might use: ```{"early_scrub": ["email","ssn","credit_card"], "early_scrub_mode":"mask_only"}```

elaine: once early-pass scrub is behind flag we'll canary it on internal tenants only and monitor for false positives. also add unit tests for nested JSON prompt shapes.

devon: small thing — telemetry schema needs a field for "capture_reason" (canary, debug-runner, manual-toggle) so we can query why a capture happened. add that to the next telemetry migration.

quentin: +1. having capture_reason will help tune quota/billing attribution.

claire: UX follow-up: include a one-click "revoke captures" action in route detail that triggers TTL=0 for that tenant-route and publishes an audit log entry.

ashok: PR up for early-scrub prototype: PTR 4321. it implements the earlier pass, masks emails, and emits `capture_reason` when capture happens. reviewers: @devon @elaine

devon: reviewing now. left minor comment about regex cost at scale. please avoid super expensive backtracking patterns.

elaine: thanks team. plan summary: rollback done, alert/dashboard TODOs assigned, early-scrub prototype in review, Console UX and audit action on roadmap. will follow up in product sync with timelines. :thumbsup:

quentin: filing the alert + runbook now. I'll ping #oncall once ready.

claire: adding console mock to next design sync.

elaine: closing thread — keeping channel updated. if anyone sees additional unexpected captures drop here.
